cases.title: The Missing Husband
cases.description: Investigate the disappearance of Holly's husband and his connection to Mark Agency.

objectives.text: Find out what happened to Holly's husband.
Investigate his work at Mark Agency.

initialItems.label: The client: Holly
initialItems.text: Holly has asked you to find her missing husband.

initialItems.label: The missing husband
initialItems.text: Holly's husband worked at Mark Agency, recovering stolen artifacts. His whereabouts are unknown.

initialItems.label: The Mark Agency connection
initialItems.text: Investigate Mark Agency to find out what happened to him. A connection is a lead, not proof.

cases.title: Dead Men Calling
cases.description: Investigate three voicemail messages that appear to contain the voice of a deceased man.

objectives.text: Read the client's email and obtain her contact details.
Review all three recent voicemail transcripts.
Complete the telephone interview with Margaret Vale.
Obtain Edward's older recordings and compare them with the recent messages.
Establish who is calling and why they want the blue folder.

initialItems.label: Dead Men Calling
initialItems.text: A widow reports receiving messages in what sounds like her late husband's voice. Read the client's email before drawing conclusions.

initialItems.label: A voice is not an identity
initialItems.text: Are the recent messages genuine speech, reused recordings, an imitation or something else? The advertisement does not establish the answer.

cases.title: The Borrowed Alibi
cases.description: Find out why three strangers claim they had dinner with the advertiser.

objectives.text: Find a way to contact the advertiser at Box 17.
Identify the people using the client's alibi.
Establish what happened on Tuesday evening.

initialItems.label: Someone has been using my alibi
initialItems.text: The advertiser claims to have eaten alone on Tuesday. Three strangers reportedly say they were having dinner with the advertiser.

initialItems.label: Three strangers
initialItems.text: Their identities and reasons for using this alibi are unknown.

cases.title: Dead Mail
cases.description: Investigate Florence Finch's false grave marker and the suspicious deliveries at Blackthorn Cemetery.

objectives.text: Inspect the delivery photograph and identify the location.
Investigate the cemetery staff and delivery records.
Complete the night observation and verify the witness.
Document the controlled delivery and submit the final report.

initialItems.label: Florence Finch — a living client
initialItems.text: Florence says a courier delivered a parcel to a grave bearing her name. Inspect the photograph and interview her before drawing conclusions.

cases.title: The Midnight Gardener
cases.description: Elder Perkins demands proof that his neighbour Olga is up to something at midnight.

objectives.text: Watch Olga's garden at midnight without waking the hound.
Take three flashless photographs of what Olga is really doing.
Deliver the evidence to Elder Perkins.

initialItems.label: The Midnight Gardener
initialItems.text: Elder Perkins claims his neighbour waters her garden at precisely midnight and wants photographic proof. He also misses his newspaper.

initialItems.label: A routine is not a crime
initialItems.text: Odd habits are not evidence. What Olga actually does at midnight remains to be established by observation.

cases.title: Mom's Not Proud
cases.description: Vincenzo Moretti wants proof of the street artist painting the town — and refuses to believe it is his daughter.

objectives.text: Stake out downtown and photograph the tagger in the act.
Establish the identity of the 'Phantom' artist.
Decide whether to give Raven to her father or protect her work.

initialItems.label: Mom's Not Proud
initialItems.text: Vincenzo Moretti, pizzeria owner, offers $150 for photographic proof of the street artist tagging the neighbourhood. He insists it is not his daughter Raven.

initialItems.label: A father's certainty
initialItems.text: Vincenzo is certain it is not Raven. Certainty without photographs is a family matter, not a case.

cases.title: Who Wears Short Shorts?
cases.description: Insurance adjuster Ray Kolpon needs clear photographs of a claimant whose spine allegedly cannot support a fork.

objectives.text: Photograph Subject #4 lifting an object over 50kg.
Photograph his face while he does it.
Deliver both photographs to Ray Kolpon.

initialItems.label: Who Wears Short Shorts?
initialItems.text: Ray Kolpon of Kolpon & Sons Adjustments offers $200 for two clear photographs of Claimant #4, who collects disability while reportedly lifting refrigerators for cardio.

initialItems.label: A report is not a spine
initialItems.text: Witnesses say he lifts refrigerators. Kolpon's paperwork says he cannot sit up. Photographs, not opinions, settle this.
